feature: Dual Authentication and Data Persistence System
workflow_rationale: This is a new feature implementation adding authentication and data persistence to the existing Auto-Claude application. Requires building backend API services, database schemas, authentication middleware, and frontend UI components. The feature follows service dependency order: backend foundation → auth API → history API → GitHub integration → frontend auth → frontend history → frontend settings → integration testing.

phases.name: Backend Foundation - Database, Models & Auth Utilities
phases.description: Set up the database layer, SQLAlchemy models for User/GitHubAccount/history types, JWT token utilities, password hashing helpers, and database migrations. This phase creates the foundational data layer that all subsequent phases depend on.

subtasks.description: Create database connection and session management module

verification.command: cd apps/backend && python -c "from database import engine, SessionLocal, Base; print('Database module loaded successfully')"

subtasks.description: Create SQLAlchemy models for User, GitHubAccount, and 4 history types (ChatHistory, IdeationHistory, RoadmapHistory, RepoHistory)

verification.command: cd apps/backend && python -c "from models import User, GitHubAccount, ChatHistory, IdeationHistory, RoadmapHistory, RepoHistory; print('All models imported successfully')"

subtasks.description: Create JWT token creation and validation utilities with 30-minute expiration
subtasks.notes: Tokens are base64 encoded NOT encrypted - never store sensitive data in payload. Use HS256 algorithm with SECRET_KEY from environment.

verification.command: cd apps/backend && python -c "from auth import create_access_token, verify_token; token = create_access_token({'data': 'test'}); print('Token created:', bool(token)); payload = verify_token(token); print('Token verified:', bool(payload))"
verification.expected:
Token created: True
Token verified: True

subtasks.description: Create password hashing and verification utilities using bcrypt
subtasks.notes: Passwords must be bytes (b'string') not strings. Hashed passwords stored as strings using .decode('utf-8'). Each hash is unique due to random salt.

verification.command: cd apps/backend && python -c "from auth import hash_password, verify_password; hashed = hash_password('testpass123'); print('Hashed:', len(hashed) > 50); verified = verify_password('testpass123', hashed); print('Verified:', verified)"

subtasks.description: Set up Alembic for database migrations and create initial migration
subtasks.notes: Alembic must be initialized with 'alembic init' command. Migration should create users, github_accounts, chat_histories, ideation_histories, roadmap_histories, repo_histories tables with proper indexes and foreign keys.

phases.name: GitHub Account Linking Backend
phases.description: Build API endpoints for linking, viewing, and unlinking GitHub accounts from user settings. This phase enables users to manage connected GitHub accounts.

subtasks.description: Create POST /github/link endpoint to link GitHub account to authenticated user
subtasks.notes:
Implemented POST /github/link endpoint in main.py:
- Added GitHubLinkRequest schema for OAuth code validation
- Endpoint exchanges OAuth code for access token using httpx
- Fetches GitHub user profile (id, username, avatar_url)
- Links account to authenticated user using link_github_account service
- Prevents duplicate github_id per user (idempotent - returns existing account)
- Returns GitHubAccountResponse with linked account info
- Proper error handling for invalid codes, GitHub API errors, and database errors
- Endpoint is protected with JWT authentication via get_current_active_user dependency

subtasks.description: Create GET /github/accounts endpoint to list user's linked GitHub accounts
subtasks.notes:
Implemented GET /github/accounts endpoint in main.py:
- Added endpoint to list all GitHub accounts linked to authenticated user
- Returns list of GitHubAccountResponse objects ordered by linked_at (newest first)
- Endpoint is protected with JWT authentication via get_current_active_user dependency
- Returns empty array when user has no linked accounts
- Comprehensive docstring with usage examples and notes
- Proper error handling for unauthorized access and server errors
- Does NOT expose access tokens in response (security measure)
- Follows existing patterns from history endpoints for consistency

subtasks.description: Create DELETE /github/unlink/{id} endpoint to unlink GitHub account
subtasks.notes:
Implemented DELETE /github/unlink/{id} endpoint in main.py:
- Added endpoint to unlink GitHub accounts from authenticated users
- Endpoint verifies account belongs to user before unlinking (via unlink_github_account service)
- Returns HTTP 204 No Content on successful deletion
- Returns HTTP 404 if account not found
- Returns HTTP 403 if account exists but belongs to different user
- Returns HTTP 500 for server errors
- Endpoint is protected with JWT authentication via get_current_active_user dependency
- Comprehensive docstring with usage examples and security notes
- Proper error handling for ValueError (ownership verification), HTTPException, and general exceptions
- Follows existing patterns from other DELETE endpoints (chat, ideation, roadmap, repo history)
- Does NOT delete user account, only the GitHub link

- Custom AuthApiError class with statusCode and details
- handleResponse() utility for consistent error handling

- Login uses URLSearchParams for OAuth2PasswordRequestForm compatibility (username field for email)

- Comprehensive JSDoc documentation with usage examples
